lines: The expansion is expected to increase annual throughput to 2.3 million tonnes, restore gold recoveries to the original design rate of 94%, and support an annual gold production target of over 200,000 ounces from the second half of 2028.

desk.headline: Sales up 17% to $293.4m; adjusted EPS $0.17 misses $0.29 estimate; production guidance reaffirmed, costs above
results: Sales rose 17% to $293.4m as the realised gold price climbed to $4,281/oz, despite slightly lower output.
Adjusted EPS was flat at $0.17; reported profit fell to $47.8m from $123.6m, which had included a $52.7m impairment reversal.
All-in sustaining cost rose to $2,286 per ounce; Séguéla output fell after a July site blockade, while Lindero output rose.
Free cash flow from ongoing operations rose to $90.8m; cash was $443.3m and liquidity $593.3m at 30 September.
Paid $200m cash for the Bambadji project in Senegal; no shares bought back in Q3 (10.8m shares, $106.6m, earlier this year).

guidance.summary: Fortuna says it remains on track for 2026 production guidance (Séguéla at the low end, Caylloma above). Costs are running above guidance: management expects full-year AISC 8–10% above the top of its range. It also approved a $109m Séguéla expansion targeting over 200,000 oz a year from H2 2028.

points: Séguéla was hit by an artisanal miners' blockade in July; management said volumes were back to plan by September.
CFO said outside factors (share-based pay, diesel, peso costs at Lindero) added about $220 per ounce to Q3 costs.
Diamba Sud permit application was accepted on 2 November; approval expected in Q4 2026 and first gold targeted mid-2028.
Growth spending of about $750m over two years comes first; management will be cautious on buybacks for two quarters.
Management expects higher production and lower, but still above-guidance, costs in Q4.
